Codex credential preflight fails while other Codex work succeeds

Multiple Codex processes can try to refresh the same native ChatGPT login. One
process may keep a rejected refresh token after another has saved a working login,
causing a credential check to report "no usable login".

Archon rechecks that result once in a fresh Codex process, using the same caller
deadline and requesting a refresh again. When the second read returns a status,
it logs

with only the resulting credential state.
The recheck does not bypass authentication or send a model request. If the recheck errors, times out or returns a malformed
response, the check is inconclusive: the run starts with a
warning, as any inconclusive credential check does.

Workflows Time Out Waiting for the First Event
A workflow node produces no output and eventually fails on a first-event timeout.
A slow environment (cold model, constrained machine) can exceed the default 60-second wait for the AI provider's first event.

Restoring the original checkout at its saved path preserves that storage root. Archon refuses automatic repair when it cannot preserve the root.
If you must move the checkout, identify and back up the existing storage root

. Work out the destination root from the new checkout's basename and migrate the existing state, artifacts and logs there as part of the move. Do not overwrite another project's storage at that destination. A path update alone does not move storage: changing the basename can hide the existing state or select a root already used by another project. Keep the original storage until you have verified the recovered project can see its state and history.
Chat Says the Working Directory No Longer Exists
A chat message in a project-scoped conversation is refused with:
This conversation's working directory no longer exists: <path>
The conversation carries a working-directory override (
) pointing at a directory that has since been removed (an isolated worktree torn down by
, the periodic reaper, the Environments list in the web UI, or your own
). The override outlives the directory. Only workflow runs re-resolve isolation; a chat turn uses the recorded path as-is.

Archon refuses the turn instead of passing the missing path to the AI provider. It does not silently fall back to the project root, because relocating the agent into the live checkout would widen its write scope without you asking for it. Before this check existed, the provider spawned into the missing directory and the failure surfaced as an unrelated error:
No such file or directory (os error 2)
and Claude reported a libc/architecture mismatch. Neither named the directory.
clears the stale override and rebinds the conversation to a project. This always works and is the suggestion you will always be offered.
when the conversation is still bound to an isolation environment. It detaches and returns you to the project root. When the environment reference has already been cleared, this command reports
This conversation is not using a worktree.
, which is why it is not suggested in that state.

The refusal writes nothing and changes no state, so a transient cause (a mount blip, a directory mid-move) costs one refused message and nothing else: the next turn re-evaluates from scratch. Operators can find these events in the logs under
, which records the conversation id, the path, and the isolation environment id.
